title: Vayeshev: God went down too (Genesis 39:2–3)
hookLine: even as a slave, "the LORD was with Joseph"

lines: THE WORST JOB YOU EVER HAD.
cards: Picture the worst job you ever had. The night shift, the rude boss, the uniform that didn't fit, the sense that this was not where your life was supposed to be. Now make it worse.
Joseph is pulled out of the pit and sold to a caravan of traders headed south. Seventeen, the favorite son, and now he's cargo.
The Torah says Joseph was brought down to Egypt, and sold as a slave to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh. Down, and down, and down.

teach.b: You might expect the next line to be about despair. Instead, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "And the LORD was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man." In the house of his Egyptian master.
Not after he was rescued. Not once things got better. There, as a slave.
The Hebrew for prosperous is matzliach, someone whose work succeeds. His master saw that God was with Joseph, and that whatever Joseph did turned out well.

teach.h: THE HOUSE BLESSED FOR HIS SAKE.
teach.b: So Potiphar puts him in charge of the whole house, and the Torah says the Egyptian's house was blessed, for Joseph's sake. Notice what Joseph does in the lowest place.
He works, well enough that a stranger notices something more than skill. He doesn't wait to be free before he's faithful. Now a promise that comes later in Genesis.

When the old Jacob is afraid to go down to Egypt himself, God tells him: "I will go down with thee into Egypt" and I'll bring you up again. God goes down too. The rabbis built a whole teaching on this.
The Talmud says that wherever Israel went into exile, the Shechinah, God's presence, went with them: into Egypt, into Babylon, into every hard place.
It's one of the most comforting ideas in Jewish thought: the lowest place is not a place God has left. It doesn't make the pit less dark, or slavery less wrong.
But Joseph, in a foreign house, with no family and no freedom, isn't alone.

how: The teaching that the Shechinah, God's presence, went with Israel into every exile is a cornerstone of Jewish comfort, taught from the Talmud and echoed in prayer and song.

o: and he settled, as the story moves into Egypt
and he prospered, Joseph's success as a slave
and he went down, Joseph brought to Egypt

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: I will go down with thee

s: the Torah says God was with Joseph only after he was freed
the LORD was with Joseph in his master's house, as a slave.
Potiphar noticed something beyond Joseph's skill
his master saw that the LORD was with him.
the Talmud says God's presence stayed behind when Israel was exiled
it says the Shechinah went with them into every exile.

games.q: you're seventeen, sold as a slave in a foreign house. you're Joseph. what do you do?
o: wait until you're free to do your best.
do good work, right where you are.
try to escape at the first chance.
games.why: Joseph worked so well that Potiphar put him over the whole house, and saw that the LORD was with him.

practice: Think of where you are right now, maybe not where you want to be, and one small piece of work in front of you: the dishes, a report, a shift. Picture doing it with care, the way Joseph did in a house that wasn't his.
If you believe it, remember that God can be in that place too.

wordCard.voice: Vayeshev. And he settled: the portion where Joseph, sold as a slave in Egypt, does good work, and the LORD was with him there.

orig.note: Hebrew: a prosperous man, one whose work succeeds. said of Joseph as a slave.

carryVoice: Your line: God goes down with you. Even into Egypt, even as a slave. See you tomorrow.
